stem: Which Indian leader for the first time used the 'Safety-Valve Theory'to attack the Moderates in the Congress?
expl: For the first time, the extremist leader Lala Lajpat Rai, in his book Young India published in 1916, used this theory to accuse the moderate leaders of the Congress of running an organisation which the British rulers were using like a “safety-valve”.

stem: Most of the moderate leaders hailed from :
expl: In the era of liberal politics or political mendicancy, most moderate leaders—such as Dadabhai Naoroji, Ferozeshah Mehta, Dinshaw Wacha, Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee and Surendranath Banerjee—were associated with urban areas. During this period, the Congress was dominated by prosperous, middle-class intellectuals, including lawyers, doctors, engineers, journalists and literary persons. Titles and high positions attracted them. The representatives who came to the Congress generally came from big cities, and their contact with the common people was limited. Ferozeshah Mehta himself said, “The voice of the Congress is not the voice of the people; however, it is the duty of other countrymen living among them to understand their feelings.

stem: Which one of the following was not an extremist?
expl: Gopal Krishna Gokhale was associated with the Liberal (Moderate) camp. He believed in equanimity and a gentle sense of justice. He had complete faith that the nation’s regeneration could not take place amid storms of agitation. He believed in the purity of both means and ends. Influenced by these ideas, Gandhiji became his disciple. He entered politics from the platform of the Bombay Congress session of 1889. In 1897, he and Dinshaw Wacha were asked to give evidence before the Welby Commission appointed to examine Indian expenditure. In 1899, he was elected to the Bombay Legislative Council and later to the Imperial Legislative Council.

stem: Indian National Movement came to be dominated by the extremists after –
expl: After 1906, within the Congress, the influence of the extremist group increased in Indian politics. The extremist group was jointly led by major Congress leaders—Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Aurobindo Ghosh.

stem: Which one of the following leaders belonged to the Extremist wing of the Congress?
expl: Aurobindo Ghosh was a leader of the extremist group in the Congress. He was one of the four pillars of the extremist group (Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Aurobindo Ghosh). In his article written in 1893–94, he said that the Congress was away from the working class, was anti-national, and had completely failed; and he described as cowardice the Congress policy of not speaking clearly due to fear of displeasing the British rulers. According to him, the Congress was going to die of tuberculosis. In 1908, the police raided Manictala Garden (another name—Murari Pukur Baganbari), arrested 14 revolutionaries, and arrested Aurobindo Ghosh from his house on Grey Street. All of them were tried in the Alipore Conspiracy Case. The trial against Aurobindo Ghosh continued for about a year, but later he was acquitted due to lack of evidence. In the course of time, he withdrew from revolutionary activities, became an ascetic, and went to Pondicherry (now Puducherry).

stem: Who propounded the doctrine of ‘Passive Resistance’?
expl: A series of articles on “Passive Resistance” was first published in the newspaper Bande Mataram between 9 and 23 April, 1907. Aurobindo Ghosh believed that the British should leave India immediately. Until the British did so, protests against them should continue.

stem: Who among the following was not known as a moderate in the National Movement?
expl: Among the four main pillars of extremism (Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Aurobindo Ghosh), Bal Gangadhar Tilak was the pioneer of this ideology. He criticized the Congress policy of petition and prayer. Tilak said about the Congress, “If we croak like frogs once a year, we will get nothing.” Dadabhai Naoroji and Gopal Krishna Gokhale were Moderate leaders of the Congress, whereas M.G. Ranade was a social reformer.

stem: Bal Gangadhar Tilak came to be known as 'Lokmanya Tilak' when –

options.label: c
options.text: The government accused him in the Rand Murder Case.

options.label: d
options.text: He started the Shivaji and Ganpati festivals.

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above.

expl: The British government made Bal Gangadhar Tilak an accused in the murder case of the then Pune plague commissioner W.C. Rand and Lieutenant Ayerst. Tilak was found guilty and was sentenced to 18 months of rigorous imprisonment. When he came out of jail, he emerged as a national hero. Thus, not due to any single incident, but after many nationalist actions, Tilak was given the title “Lokmanya.”

stem: Who said, “Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it”?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The slogan, “Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it,” associated with Bal Gangadhar Tilak, has been a subject of considerable disagreement among scholars regarding when Tilak first used it. In fact, the idea of this slogan began to take shape in the 1890s. Scholars believe that Tilak’s close associate, Joseph “Kaka” Baptista, first coined this sentence. It is believed that Baptista probably composed this line in Marathi—“Swarajya ha maza janmasiddha hakk ahe, ani to mi milavnarach”—and Tilak adopted it and carried it to the masses. On the basis of available evidence, it can be said that Tilak used this slogan from public platforms during the Home Rule Movement in April–May 1916. Some sources emphasize that Tilak used this slogan at the Lucknow session of the Congress in 1916, but sufficient historical evidence in support of this is not available.

stem: In 1908, Bal Gangadhar Tilak was imprisoned for –
expl: In 1908, on the basis of articles published in ‘Kesari’, Tilak was tried for sedition and was sentenced to 6 years of transportation/exile along with a fine of Rs. 1000, and he was sent to Mandalay Jail (Myanmar).

stem: The protest method of moderate leaders of the Congress was?
expl: The chief method of agitation of the moderate leaders of the Congress was constitutional agitation, i.e., demanding Indians’ participation in administration and creating political awareness among the people.

Lala Lajpat Rai was also known as “Sher-e-Punjab.” He was a leader of the extremist faction in the Indian National Congress and a representative of the whole of Punjab. He is also called “Punjab Kesari.” While leading a procession in protest against the Simon Commission, Lala Ji was injured due to lathi blows; as a result, he passed away on 17 November 1928.
